title: Let the host app supply its own permission policy
narrative: Fangore’s product needs a host app whose permission rules are defined by the application, not by copying grant lists into every agent constructor. He configures the harness once so the app’s composed permission packs — as in `fangore_compound_grants` — are what the harness enforces. Success: the injected access control already honors those packs. He uses this whenever a host must stay configuration-first instead of sprinkling grants by hand.
implementation: `MechaHarnessConfig` (pyiv) owns DI wiring. Hosts subclass Config and override `get_access_policy()` to return an `AccessPolicy` or `CompoundPolicy`; `get_access_control()` builds `AccessControl` from that policy and the event log. Default `get_grants()` is deny-by-default empty. This is the library extension point for host permission packs — not a service locator bag of grants on `Settings`.
validation: Kind `config_access_policy` → `_run_config_access_policy`. Soft expects: injector-resolved `AccessControl` honors the host `CompoundPolicy`. Related: `tests/test_di.py`, access/compound policy unit tests.
